text: {"changed_files": ["lib/cmdline.c"], "summary": "In get_range() (lib/cmdline.c), the range expansion wrote values with `*pint--` so the output pointer moved backwards, producing zeros at the expected positions; changing it to `*pint++` restores forward filling so cmdline_test_range passes."}

text: {"changed_files": ["lib/kstrtox.c"], "summary": "_parse_integer_limit() in lib/kstrtox.c had its digit-validity check changed from `val >= base` to `val > base`, so letter digits equal to the base (e.g. 'a' in base 10) were parsed as numbers; restoring `val >= base` fixes simple_strtoull/get_options parsing and the cmdline_test_range failures."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/kstrtox.c"], "summary": "The seed commit inverted the leading-zero check in `_parse_integer_fixup_radix` (`s[0] != '0'` instead of `s[0] == '0'`), so base-0 integer parsing in `get_options`/`get_range` misread decimal input like \"4-8\" and returned 0 numbers; restoring the original condition fixes the cmdline range test."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/string_helpers.c"], "summary": "In unescape_octal() the shift was written as `num << 3;` (a no-op expression, which is also what GCC warned about) instead of `num <<= 3;`, so multi-digit octal escapes were decoded wrongly (e.g. \\387 yielded 55 instead of 56); changed it to the compound assignment."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/string_helpers.c"], "summary": "In unescape_hex() the 'x' check used `*q--`, which moved the pointer back onto the backslash so every \\xHH escape was rejected; changing it to `*q++` lets hex escapes decode, which fixes the length mismatch in test_unescape."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/string_helpers.c"], "summary": "escape_passthrough() advanced the output pointer by 2 instead of 1 for each passed-through character, over-counting the escaped length in the ESCAPE_NP/NA/NAP cases; changed it to `out + 1`."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/string_helpers.c"], "summary": "In escape_space(), the `--out` before writing the escape letter made it overwrite the previous output byte and emit no escape sequence for \\n, \\r, \\t, \\v, \\f; changing it to `++out` (matching escape_special/escape_octal) fixes the escape 0 length mismatch in string_helpers_kunit."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/string_helpers.c"], "summary": "escape_special() decremented the output pointer (`--out`) instead of advancing it after writing the two-character escape sequence, so string_escape_mem() returned a too-short length; changed it to `++out` so the escaped length matches the test's expected 27 bytes."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/string_helpers.c"], "summary": "In escape_null(), the output pointer was rewound with `--out` after writing the two-byte `\\0` escape, so NUL bytes emitted only one byte of output; changing it to `++out` restores the correct length that test_unescape's \"escape 0\" check expects."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/string_helpers.c"], "summary": "In escape_octal(), a stray `--out` before the second digit made each octal escape write only 3 characters instead of 4 and overwrite the backslash and first digit, so I removed it to restore the four-character `\\NNN` output that the \"escape 0\" test expects."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/string_helpers.c"], "summary": "escape_hex() in lib/string_helpers.c had a stray `--out;` after writing 'x', so each \\xHH escape was emitted one byte short (the 14 vs 18 mismatch in the \"escape 0\" case); removing it restores the upstream behaviour."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/cmdline.c"], "summary": "In lib/cmdline.c, get_option() used `--cur` instead of `++cur` when skipping a leading '-', so negative numbers were not parsed, and get_options() broke out of its loop on any return code other than 1, so a comma (2) or a range (3) ended parsing early; the fix is `++cur` and continuing on `res == 2 || res == 3`."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/cmdline.c"], "summary": "In get_range() (lib/cmdline.c), the expanded range values were written with `*pint--`, which moved the output pointer backwards; changed it to `*pint++` so ranges like `0-1` fill the array forwards, matching the expected values in the failing test cases."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/cmdline.c"], "summary": "In get_option(), a leading '-' was handled with `--cur` (pre-decrement), so the number was parsed from the character before the '-' rather than the digits after it; changing it to `++cur` fixes the negative-number parsing that broke test cases 14 and 18 of cmdline_test_range."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/cmdline.c"], "summary": "In get_option() (lib/cmdline.c), a leading '-' was handled with `simple_strtoull(--cur, ...)`, which parsed from the byte before the minus sign and so produced wrong values and ranges; changing it to `++cur` makes the number parse after the '-' as intended, which fixes the cmdline_test_range expectations."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/string_helpers.c"], "summary": "Fixed two bugs in lib/string_helpers.c: string_get_size() decremented the exponent when reducing a huge size (i-- should be i++, which caused the 'UNK' unit output), and string_escape_mem() read its input backwards (*src-- should be *src++), which caused the escape test mismatches."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/string_helpers.c"], "summary": "In string_unescape(), the escape-sequence guard tested `src[1] == '\\0'` instead of `src[1] != '\\0'`, so backslash escapes were never decoded (only a trailing lone backslash was), making the output one byte longer per escape and failing test_unescape; the condition is now inverted to match upstream."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/string_helpers.c"], "summary": "Fixed two inverted checks in lib/string_helpers.c: string_get_size() decremented the exponent `i` when reducing `size` (it must increment, like the blk_size loop, so huge values stop yielding \"UNK\"), and string_unescape() tested `src[1] == '\\0'` instead of `!= '\\0'`, so backslash escapes were never processed."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/string_helpers.c"], "summary": "Fixed two bugs in lib/string_helpers.c: string_get_size() decremented the exponent `i` in its size-reduction loop instead of incrementing it (causing a negative index and the \"UNK\"/garbage unit output for U64_MAX), and escape_passthrough() advanced the output pointer by 2 instead of 1 (doubling pass-through escape output length)."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/string.c"], "summary": "strncasecmp() in lib/string.c read the first string with `*s1--` (walking backwards) instead of `*s1++`, so it compared the wrong bytes; changed it to `*s1++` to match the forward advance of s2."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/siphash.c"], "summary": "The 64-bit `__siphash_aligned` and `__hsiphash_aligned` functions computed the tail length with `len & (sizeof(u64) - 2)`, which drops bit 0 and miscounts tail bytes for lengths with `len % 8` equal to 1 or 7; changed both to `sizeof(u64) - 1` to match the unaligned variants."}
